FINDER F4b, PART 3f: NETWORK-WAIT WINDOWS IN THE NEW PRODUCT JOURNEY, AND TWO STALE GATE STATEMENTS. Work on this branch only (feat/finder-f4b, now at 0415d352, which already merges current main). Do not change application code under apps/web/src in this part.

BACKGROUND. The reviewer ran apps/web/cypress/e2e/product-journey.cy.ts locally with the cypress-parity.yml setup and VITE_FINDER_F4_ENABLED=1, on a tree identical to this branch's code. Part 3e worked: the clean-session load now calls GET /api/v1/systems/9007199254740993 every time, and the three existing journeys pass. The new journey ("ranks the pinned Flexible B corpus, retains URL selection and restores Finder history") failed all three attempts, each at a different place: (1) a location check in assertFinderUrl right after selecting the result on page 0; (2) the 14th `cy.wait('@rankings')` (Forward to min-tier A, offset 1) — the fetch was visibly in flight just after the window closed; (3) "cy.wait() timed out waiting 5000ms for the 9th request to the route: rankings. No request ever occurred" (Back to min-tier A, offset 0). A Playwright probe without Cypress, on the same flag-on build, measured the delay from each user action to the rankings request: tier change 5.0 s, Next 6.2 s, Back 1.8-2.0 s, Forward 1.9-3.1 s, with 3.9-5.8 s of main-thread long tasks per action and none while idle (SwiftShader WebGL on 2 CPUs). So the requests are made, correctly, but later than the default 5-second `requestTimeout` on a slow software-GL machine. CI runners are about 3-6x faster (CI run 41270898063: the unsafe-id64 journey took 6.7 s in Chrome and 16.4 s in Firefox, against 100 s locally), which leaves Firefox in CI little margin over 5 s. The spec already gives its DOM and location checks explicit 15-20 s windows for the same reason.

CHANGE 1 (apps/web/cypress/e2e/product-journey.cy.ts). Give every network wait that the new journey performs an explicit `requestTimeout: 20_000`: the `cy.wait('@rankings')` in assertRankingsRequest, the `cy.wait('@search')` in assertAnyPage, and the `cy.wait('@selectedPoint')` after the clean-session load. Use one named constant for the 20-second request window, next to the other shared helpers at the top of the file, and use it in those three places. Keep every assertion, every request-count expectation and the order of waits exactly as they are; only the waiting window changes. Leave the waits in the other journeys alone unless they go through those same helpers. Do not add retries, `cy.wait(<milliseconds>)` sleeps, or intercept stubs. The Product lane must keep observing real API traffic only.

CHANGE 2 (docs, the F4b CHANGES.md entry dated 2026-11-01 and the "Status update — 2026-11-01" paragraph in section 1 of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-v3-finder-f4-archetype-ui-design.md). Both currently say that every gate before enabling F4 in a governed production or release build is unchanged, and list among those gates the step 9′ product-publication sequence and slice 1c's representative-scale proof. Both of those are now met, and the merged main says so: docs/ROADMAP.md records "Finder LIVE — step 9′ complete (2026-10-23)", and the design's own "Status update — 2026-10-31" paragraph directly above records that slice 1c's proof passed all 72 measurements (receipt docs/operations/evidence/2026-10-31-v3-finder-slice1c-rankings-scale-proof-receipt.json). Rewrite those two passages so they state, accurately and briefly: the migration, build and step 9′ product-publication sequence is complete (2026-10-23) and slice 1c's proof has passed (2026-10-31); what still has to happen before the flag may be enabled in any governed production or release build is F4c, F4e and the separate governed application-release gate (read section 1 and section 8 of the design and keep any other remaining gate they name, such as visual approval); and nothing in F4b enables the flag in such a build or authorizes a deployment. The design's status paragraph also says F4b "is implemented on `feat/finder-f4b`"; reword it so it stays true after the branch merges (for example "F4b is implemented behind the default-off ..."). Do not edit any other dated status paragraph or older CHANGES entry; they are history. Do not change the undated design text below the status paragraphs.

VALIDATION before you finish. In apps/web: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`. Then run the Python contract tests that read these files: `grep -rln "product-journey\|2026-10-10-v3-finder-f4-archetype-ui-design\|Finder F4b" tests` and run every test module it lists with pytest, plus tests/test_seed_cypress_v3_generation.py. If any contract test pins the exact sentences you changed, update it to assert the new, accurate statement rather than restoring the stale text. Report the commands and their results, and list every line you changed in the spec.
